questions.q: Under the shared responsibility model for IaaS, which component is ALWAYS the cloud customer's responsibility?
choices: Physical security of the data center
Hypervisor hardening
Guest operating system patching and configuration
Underlying network fabric maintenance
questions.why: In IaaS the provider secures the hardware and hypervisor, but the customer owns the guest OS, its patching, and configuration.

questions.q: As you move from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, how does the customer's share of security responsibility change?
choices: It shifts entirely to the customer in SaaS
It stays constant across all service models
It generally decreases as the provider assumes more of the stack
It increases because more services are exposed
questions.why: SaaS puts the most responsibility on the provider, so the customer's portion shrinks moving from IaaS to SaaS.

questions.q: Which cloud characteristic defined by NIST allows customers to provision compute without human interaction from the provider?
choices: Rapid elasticity
Measured service
On-demand self-service
Resource pooling
questions.why: On-demand self-service lets consumers provision capabilities automatically without requiring provider staff involvement.

questions.q: A financial firm needs dedicated, single-tenant hardware but still wants cloud provisioning. Which deployment model best fits?
choices: Multi-cloud brokerage
Community cloud
Private cloud
Public cloud
questions.why: A private cloud is provisioned for exclusive use by a single organization, giving single-tenant isolation with cloud provisioning.

questions.q: What is the primary security concern that multitenancy introduces in public cloud environments?
choices: Reduced elasticity during peak load
Isolation failure allowing one tenant to access another's data
Loss of measured service billing accuracy
Higher latency from resource pooling
questions.why: Multitenancy raises the risk that weak logical isolation lets one tenant reach another tenant's data or workloads.

questions.q: Which term describes the risk of being unable to easily move workloads and data from one cloud provider to another?
choices: Resource pooling
Tenant sprawl
Elastic contention
Vendor lock-in
questions.why: Vendor lock-in occurs when proprietary formats or services make migration to another provider difficult and costly.

questions.q: In cloud reference architecture, what is the role of a cloud access broker or cloud service broker?
choices: A device that decrypts all tenant traffic at the hypervisor
An intermediary that manages use, performance, and delivery of cloud services
A hardware appliance that stores encryption keys on-prem
A provider tool that meters billing only
questions.why: A cloud service broker mediates relationships between consumers and providers, adding value to service use and delivery.

questions.q: Which emerging technology concern involves securely running code without managing the underlying servers?
choices: Physical tamper detection
Serverless (Function as a Service) security
Hypervisor introspection
Bare-metal provisioning
questions.why: Serverless / FaaS abstracts servers away, shifting focus to function permissions, event triggers, and dependencies.

questions.q: What does the term 'reversibility' refer to in cloud service agreements?
choices: The provider's ability to roll back a failed deployment
The capacity to undo an encryption operation
The ability to retrieve data and terminate service, restoring the prior state
The customer's right to reverse a billing charge
questions.why: Reversibility is the process of reclaiming assets and data so the customer can revert to a state before the cloud engagement.

questions.q: Which order correctly represents the phases of the cloud secure data lifecycle?
choices: Create, Use, Store, Archive, Share, Destroy
Store, Create, Share, Use, Destroy, Archive
Ingest, Process, Encrypt, Share, Retain, Purge
Create, Store, Use, Share, Archive, Destroy
questions.why: The recognized cloud data lifecycle proceeds Create, Store, Use, Share, Archive, then Destroy.

questions.q: In a Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) arrangement, who generates and controls the master key material?
choices: The hypervisor derives keys automatically per tenant
The provider generates the key and shares it with the customer
A third-party escrow agent generates keys for both parties
The customer generates the key and imports it into the provider's KMS
questions.why: BYOK lets the customer create key material externally and import it into the cloud KMS, retaining more control over provenance.

questions.q: What is the main security benefit of tokenization compared with encryption for protecting card data?
choices: Tokens are always shorter and faster to transmit
Tokens can be reversed without any lookup table
The token has no mathematical relationship to the original value, removing systems from PCI scope
Tokenization requires no key management at all
questions.why: A token is a surrogate value with no algorithmic link to the original, so token-only systems can fall outside PCI scope.

questions.q: Which technique lets data be processed while it remains encrypted, without decrypting it first?
choices: Transparent data encryption
Homomorphic encryption
Format-preserving encryption
Client-side field masking
questions.why: Homomorphic encryption permits computation directly on ciphertext, producing an encrypted result matching operations on plaintext.

questions.q: A DLP solution in the cloud is being deployed to inspect files leaving object storage. Which DLP component performs the actual policy matching?
choices: The discovery crawler only
The tenant billing meter
The key management service
The detection/analysis engine
questions.why: DLP has discovery, monitoring, and enforcement stages; the detection engine analyzes content against policy to decide action.

questions.q: Why is cryptographic erasure (crypto-shredding) especially useful for data destruction in the cloud?
choices: It physically degausses the provider's shared disks
Destroying the keys renders encrypted data unrecoverable without physical media access
It guarantees NIST purge on multitenant SSDs directly
It removes the need to encrypt data at rest
questions.why: In shared storage you cannot physically destroy media, so deleting the encryption keys makes the ciphertext permanently unreadable.

questions.q: Where does client-side encryption place the encryption operation relative to the cloud provider?
choices: Encryption happens inside the hypervisor at write time
Data is encrypted before it reaches the provider, so the provider never sees plaintext
The KMS decrypts data for indexing then re-encrypts
The provider encrypts data as it lands in storage
questions.why: Client-side encryption performs the crypto operation before upload, keeping keys and plaintext away from the provider.

questions.q: An Information Rights Management (IRM) solution primarily protects data by doing what?
choices: Replacing sensitive fields with random tokens
Blocking all outbound network traffic from the tenant
Embedding access controls and usage restrictions that travel with the file
Encrypting only data at rest in object storage
questions.why: IRM binds persistent access and usage policies to the document itself so controls remain enforced wherever the file goes.

questions.q: Which key management model gives the customer the strongest control by keeping keys entirely outside the provider's KMS?
choices: Envelope encryption using the provider's root key
Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) with an external key store
BYOK with keys imported to the provider KMS
Provider-managed default keys
questions.why: HYOK keeps keys in a customer-controlled external HSM or key store, so the provider never possesses usable key material.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a hardware security module (HSM) in cloud key management?
choices: A tamper-resistant device that generates, stores, and protects cryptographic keys
A logging appliance for audit trails
A virtual switch that isolates tenant VLANs
A load balancer that distributes encrypted traffic
questions.why: An HSM is a hardened, tamper-resistant device dedicated to secure key generation, storage, and cryptographic operations.

questions.q: In cloud infrastructure, what does the management plane primarily control?
choices: The actual application traffic between users and workloads
The tenant's guest OS antivirus signatures
Provisioning, configuration, and orchestration of cloud resources
Physical HVAC and power in the data center
questions.why: The management plane orchestrates and configures resources; compromising it can affect the entire cloud environment.

questions.q: Why is protecting the cloud management plane considered critical?
choices: It only affects billing accuracy
It handles physical badge access to the facility
Its compromise can allow control over many or all tenant resources at once
It stores customer plaintext data by default
questions.why: The management plane has broad orchestration power, so a breach there can cascade across large portions of the environment.

questions.q: Which control best mitigates the risk of a VM escape (guest breaking out to the hypervisor)?
choices: Storing snapshots in the same tenant bucket
Increasing the guest VM's RAM allocation
Keeping the hypervisor patched and minimizing its attack surface
Disabling tenant network segmentation
questions.why: VM escape targets hypervisor flaws, so timely hypervisor patching and hardening are the primary defenses.

questions.q: A micro-segmentation strategy in a cloud virtual network is intended to achieve what?
choices: Automatic key rotation for at-rest data
Faster north-south internet egress
Granular east-west traffic control between workloads to limit lateral movement
Reduced storage costs through deduplication
questions.why: Micro-segmentation applies fine-grained policies between workloads, restricting lateral movement if one host is compromised.

questions.q: What is the main goal of a cloud business continuity and disaster recovery plan's Recovery Time Objective (RTO)?
choices: The maximum acceptable time to restore a service after disruption
The frequency of full backups
The time to rotate encryption keys
The maximum acceptable data loss measured in time
questions.why: RTO defines how quickly a service must be restored; RPO, by contrast, defines tolerable data loss.

questions.q: Which measure defines the maximum tolerable amount of data loss, expressed as a point in time, for cloud DR?
choices: Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD)
Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
Mean Time to Repair (MTTR)
questions.why: RPO specifies how much data, in time, can be lost, guiding backup and replication frequency.

questions.q: In securing container orchestration, what is a key benefit of running containers as non-root?
choices: It removes the need for network policies
It limits the blast radius if a container is compromised
It speeds up image pull times
It encrypts the container filesystem automatically
questions.why: Running as non-root reduces privileges available to an attacker who breaks into a container, containing the impact.

questions.q: A Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tool primarily helps organizations do what?
choices: Continuously detect misconfigurations and compliance drift across cloud resources
Provide runtime memory forensics on VMs
Tokenize cardholder data before storage
Encrypt application-layer traffic in transit
questions.why: CSPM continuously assesses cloud configurations against policy and best practice, flagging misconfigurations and drift.

questions.q: Which physical/environmental design concept ensures a data center has no single point of failure in power and cooling?
choices: Single-homed utility feeds
Removing environmental monitoring to reduce cost
Consolidating all UPS into one unit
Redundancy of critical infrastructure (e.g., N+1)
questions.why: Redundant designs like N+1 provide backup capacity for power and cooling, eliminating single points of failure.

questions.q: When performing threat modeling for a cloud application, which framework categorizes threats as Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, and Elevation of privilege?
choices: OCTAVE
STRIDE
PASTA
DREAD
questions.why: STRIDE is the threat classification model covering those six categories, widely used in application threat modeling.

questions.q: In a secure cloud SDLC, static application security testing (SAST) is best characterized as what?
choices: Testing the running application by sending malicious inputs
Scanning container images for outdated packages only
Analyzing source or bytecode for vulnerabilities without executing it
Reviewing production logs for anomalies
questions.why: SAST inspects code statically for flaws before execution, catching issues early in development.

questions.q: Which testing approach evaluates a running cloud application from the outside by sending inputs and observing responses?
choices: Dynamic application security testing (DAST)
Static application security testing (SAST)
Software composition analysis (SCA)
Interactive threat modeling
questions.why: DAST tests the live application externally, probing runtime behavior without access to source code.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Software Composition Analysis (SCA) in cloud application security?
choices: Load testing the API gateway
Rotating service account credentials
Identifying vulnerabilities and license risks in open-source and third-party components
Encrypting data before it is written to storage
questions.why: SCA inventories third-party and open-source dependencies to flag known vulnerabilities and licensing concerns.

questions.q: In the context of APIs, why is proper authentication and rate limiting important for cloud applications?
choices: They eliminate the need for TLS on endpoints
APIs are a primary attack surface and can be abused for data exposure or DoS
They reduce the size of JSON payloads
They automatically classify data at rest
questions.why: Cloud APIs are heavily exposed; strong auth and rate limiting curb credential abuse, scraping, and denial-of-service.

questions.q: Which OWASP concern is most directly addressed by validating and sanitizing all user input in a cloud web app?
choices: Injection attacks
Security misconfiguration of storage
Weak key management
Insufficient logging
questions.why: Input validation and sanitization are the core defenses against injection flaws such as SQL and command injection.

questions.q: What is the security value of using immutable infrastructure and infrastructure-as-code in cloud deployments?
choices: It removes the need for identity management
It guarantees zero downtime during attacks
It encrypts all secrets automatically at runtime
Consistent, version-controlled configurations reduce drift and unauthorized changes
questions.why: IaC and immutable builds enforce repeatable, reviewable configurations, minimizing configuration drift and ad hoc changes.

questions.q: A sandbox is used in cloud application development primarily to do what?
choices: Isolate and test code or untrusted components away from production
Replace the need for code review
Store production encryption keys
Serve as the primary CDN cache
questions.why: A sandbox provides an isolated environment to test code and untrusted components without risking production systems.

questions.q: Why should secrets like API keys never be hardcoded in application source stored in a cloud repository?
choices: Exposed repositories can leak the secrets, enabling unauthorized access
Hardcoding increases application latency
It violates the data residency principle
Source control cannot store text values
questions.why: Hardcoded secrets in repos are frequently leaked; a secrets manager should store and inject them at runtime instead.

questions.q: In cloud IAM, what does federated identity primarily enable?
choices: Using a single set of credentials from a trusted identity provider across multiple services
Encrypting tokens at rest in object storage
Storing all passwords in the application database
Bypassing multi-factor authentication for admins
questions.why: Federation lets an identity provider assert authentication to relying services, enabling single sign-on across domains.

questions.q: Which protocol is most commonly used to exchange authentication and authorization assertions between an IdP and a cloud SaaS service provider?
choices: SCTP
SAML
SMTP
SNMP
questions.why: SAML is the XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization assertions in federated SSO.

questions.q: A CASB (Cloud Access Security Broker) sits between users and cloud services mainly to provide what?
choices: Hypervisor patch management
Bare-metal server provisioning
Physical access control to the data center
Visibility, compliance, data security, and threat protection for cloud usage
questions.why: A CASB enforces policy between users and cloud apps across the pillars of visibility, compliance, data security, and threat protection.

questions.q: What is the main challenge of digital forensics in a public cloud environment?
choices: Guest VMs cannot be snapshotted
Chain of custody does not apply to virtual evidence
Limited access to underlying hardware and multitenant data commingling
Logs are never generated by cloud services
questions.why: Cloud forensics is hard because customers lack physical hardware access and data may share media with other tenants.

questions.q: During cloud incident response, why is preserving volatile data especially difficult?
choices: Elastic resources may be terminated automatically, destroying memory and state
Providers always block all evidence collection
Volatile data is irrelevant to cloud investigations
Cloud VMs have no memory to capture
questions.why: Auto-scaling and ephemeral instances can be torn down quickly, erasing volatile memory before it is captured.

questions.q: Which practice ensures cloud audit logs can be trusted as evidence and are protected from tampering?
choices: Disabling log forwarding to reduce cost
Storing logs on the same instance that generates them
Allowing administrators to edit logs for clarity
Writing logs to a separate, immutable, access-controlled store
questions.why: Centralized, immutable, access-controlled log storage preserves integrity and supports evidentiary and audit needs.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system in cloud operations?
choices: Encrypting object storage buckets automatically
Managing DNS records for tenant domains
Aggregating and correlating logs and events to detect and investigate incidents
Provisioning new virtual machines on demand
questions.why: A SIEM collects and correlates log and event data across sources to enable detection, alerting, and investigation.

questions.q: In cloud operations, what does a change management process primarily protect against?
choices: Unauthorized or untested modifications that could cause outages or vulnerabilities
Loss of encryption keys in the HSM
Physical theft of servers
Excessive network bandwidth billing
questions.why: Change management ensures modifications are reviewed, approved, and tested, reducing risk of outages and introduced weaknesses.

questions.q: Why does patching in a shared cloud environment often rely on the provider for certain layers?
choices: The provider controls the hypervisor and physical infrastructure the customer cannot touch
Customers are contractually forbidden from patching anything
Cloud systems never require patching
Patches are applied only through the billing console
questions.why: In shared responsibility, the provider patches layers like the hypervisor and hardware that customers cannot access.

questions.q: What is the main operational benefit of using a baseline configuration for cloud virtual machines?
choices: A known-good, hardened starting point that eases detection of deviations
It eliminates the need for identity controls
It guarantees compliance with all global laws
It removes the need for any monitoring
questions.why: A hardened baseline provides a consistent secure standard, making it easier to spot and remediate configuration deviations.

questions.q: Which concept requires that personal data be stored and processed within a specific country's borders?
choices: Data minimization
Data localization / data residency
Data portability
Data masking
questions.why: Data localization or residency mandates that data physically remain within defined geographic or jurisdictional boundaries.

questions.q: Under the GDPR, an organization that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data is called the what?
choices: Data processor
Data subject
Data controller
Data custodian
questions.why: GDPR defines the controller as the entity deciding the purposes and means of processing; the processor acts on its behalf.

questions.q: Which audit report type is designed to be freely shared and describes controls without detailed test results, useful for marketing to prospects?
choices: SOC 1 Type 1
SOC 3
SOC 1 Type 2
SOC 2 Type 2
questions.why: SOC 3 is a general-use report suitable for public distribution, unlike the restricted-use detailed SOC 2 reports.

questions.q: What distinguishes a SOC 2 Type 2 report from a SOC 2 Type 1 report?
choices: Type 2 is a public marketing document
Type 2 is only about financial reporting controls
Type 2 omits any control testing
Type 2 tests operating effectiveness of controls over a period, not just design at a point in time
questions.why: SOC 2 Type 2 evaluates whether controls operated effectively over a period, while Type 1 assesses design at a single point.

questions.q: In cloud contracts, what does an SLA primarily define?
choices: The provider's internal source code
The encryption algorithms used for data at rest
Measurable service commitments such as availability and associated remedies
The customer's marketing obligations
questions.why: An SLA sets measurable performance commitments like uptime and defines remedies or penalties for missing them.

questions.q: Which risk treatment option is being used when an organization purchases cyber insurance to offset potential cloud breach losses?
choices: Risk transference
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance
Risk mitigation
questions.why: Buying insurance shifts financial impact to a third party, which is the risk transference strategy.

questions.q: When a cloud contract ends, why is a documented data retention and deletion clause important for compliance?
choices: It selects the tenant's encryption keys
It defines the hypervisor patch schedule
It ensures data is returned or destroyed per legal and regulatory obligations
It sets the provider's stock price
questions.why: Clear retention and deletion terms ensure data is returned or securely destroyed to meet legal and regulatory duties.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) before deploying a new cloud processing activity?
choices: To select the container orchestration platform
To benchmark network throughput
To identify and mitigate privacy risks to data subjects before processing begins
To calculate the provider's monthly bill
questions.why: A DPIA systematically evaluates and mitigates privacy risks to individuals prior to high-risk processing activities.
